name: Multi-brand
summary: Customer screens for several brands, often on phones: sign-up, checkout, account. Components never change; brand primitives do.
description: Multi-brand is an Open DS scheme: a full set of answers to the Open DS grammar, with the reasons behind each, usage rules, voice and tone, and the tokens that follow. Customer screens for several brands, often on phones: sign-up, checkout, account. Components never change; brand primitives do.

ai.use_when: Companies that sell to customers under several brands, or white-label products shown to their clients' customers: sign-up, checkout, account and product pages.
ai.avoid_when: A single product with one brand, where the brand layer is cost with no user; or tools staff use all day. Use Dense data for those.

scenarios.text: A customer signs up for a plan on the Birch site, then manages it in the shared account area.
A product team launches a fourth brand by adding brand primitives, without touching components.

summary.text: A plain shared voice. Each brand adds its own tone on top, never its own structure.

principles.text: Shared structure: object, state, next step.

out.why: Multi-brand draws on core, content and media families, not conversation. It admits only families in its roles. Its only messages go to support through a textarea.
Multi-brand draws on core, content and media families, not conversation. It admits only families in its roles. Its only messages go to support through a textarea.
Multi-brand draws on core, content and media families, not data. It admits only families in its roles. Its scenarios are signing up and managing a plan.
Command suits expert users who jump anywhere by typing, not people who visit now and then. Multi-brand's customers return now and then, and most visits last a few minutes.
Right-click menus suit power users, and people who don't know to right-click never find them. Multi-brand's customers see it fresh each time. Plan actions sit in a visible menu.
Multi-brand draws on core, content and media families, not data. It avoids tools staff use all day and points those to Dense data.
Hover cards need a mouse, and touch screens have no hover. Multi-brand's customers use any device. A popover opens plan details by tap.
Multi-brand draws on core, content and media families, not conversation. It admits only families in its roles. Its only messages go to support through a textarea.
Menubar suits dense desktop tools, not website navigation or phones. Brand sites use navigation-menu, and customers sign up on phones.

color.$description: Color options: raw hue ramps. Each hue has a light ramp and a dark ramp (the same steps tuned for dark backgrounds). Steps only: each theme decides its own base (@). Themes pick from these; components never read them.

slate-deep.$description: The slate-deep hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.
